bullets.title: Hot Core CPI sparks rate-hike repricing; 10Y yields volatile at 5.08-5.19%
bullets.body: September core CPI came in at 0.335% MoM unrounded (vs. 0.2% Street, 0.18% Feroli), pushing Fed odds for an October hike above 50% before settling back to ~32% with ~30bp of hikes priced through year-end. Treasury 10Y spiked then reversed to ~5.19% as markets debated whether the inflation shock is demand-destructive (stagflation thesis) rather than persistent. Real average hourly earnings fell 0.7% YoY as wage growth (3%) lagged inflation (3.7%) for six straight months.

bullets.title: AI credit stress dominates tape: CRWV bonds at 78¢/15% yield, neocloud CDS blowing out
bullets.body: CoreWeave unsecured bonds traded below 80¢ with yields above 15%, sparking broad AI infrastructure de-risking. Hedge funds de-grossed -1.3std in US equities; the AI complex saw -1.9std long selling including -1.5std hyperscalers and -0.8std semis. IMF flagged $300B equity + $650B debt pledged against $1.4T promised AI revenue as systemic risk; Gartner separately estimated $3.5T AI infrastructure at impairment risk by 2030 if 12% ROIC not achieved.

bullets.title: Semis/SOX 7th down day: -4.3% session; Asia devastated with Kospi -7%, SK Hynix -12.7%
bullets.body: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index extended its losing streak, on pace to erase over $1T in market cap over six sessions. Asian semis bore the brunt: Samsung -10.78%, SK Hynix -12.7%, Kioxia -12%, Advantest -15%. US premarket: WDC -5.7%, SNDK -5.2%, DELL -12%, COHR -8.9%, CRDO -8.5%, ANET -5%, MU -4.3%. SOX sits ~20% off July lows and ~15% below June ATHs; positioning at 46th percentile vs. 19th percentile lows in July.

bullets.title: TSMC posts 6th straight record quarter; raises FY26 revenue growth guide to +44% on AI demand
bullets.body: TSMC reported 3Q revenue of $46.7B (vs. $45.4B consensus), with gross margin of 66.4%. Q4 revenue guided to $52.3-54.3B (vs. $50.1B consensus), implying +14% QoQ. FY26 revenue growth upgraded to ~44% YoY (vs. 40% prior); AI accelerator revenue expected to grow mid-to-high 50%+ CAGR. N2 represented ~8% of quarterly wafer revenue and capacity is set to more than double in CY27. Overseas fab construction remains a 200-400bps gross margin headwind expanding over time.

bullets.title: Mag7 outperforms semis for 8 consecutive sessions; SaaS/Apps relative strength emerges
bullets.body: As semi/hardware dollars rotated into mega-cap growth, INTU +2.98%, ADBE +1.86%, NOW +0.99% outperformed on the session. Jefferies notes tech sell skew hit 8-month highs (2.6σ) ahead of Anthropic news with record puts traded in CRWV. Defensive large-caps AAPL and HUBS also outperforming early. Nasdaq futures down ~100-110bps premarket; S&P futures mixed at -0.3% to +0.32% depending on source/timing.

bullets.title: Anthropic Q3 revenue $16.8B, cash-flow positive — but market disappointed by lack of S-1 disclosure
bullets.body: Anthropic reported Q3 revenue of $16.8B, tracking toward its $100B ARR run-rate target, with EBIT slightly positive continuing Q2 trajectory. Stock sold off sharply despite being in-line with expectations — market reaction driven by absence of new S-1 disclosure beyond headline number. Concern that AI equity weakness could make IPO timing less favorable, though capital investments in AI buildout are unlikely to reverse overnight.

bullets.title: AI buildout phase shifting to 'broadening': software/adopters gaining value share from infrastructure
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley frames AI as transitioning from buildout to broadening phase, with infrastructure enablers still benefiting but software and AI adopters beginning to capture more value. Hyperscaler capex trajectory supports this: top-4 tracking $710B+ in CY26, potentially $1.3T in CY27 vs. $375B in CY25. However, hyperscaler FCF expected to trough near zero in 2026-27, raising the question of external financing for the next capex stage.

bullets.title: Smartphone shipments -22% YoY in worst September-quarter decline; memory cost surge hits hardware
bullets.body: Global smartphone shipments fell 22% YoY in 3Q26 (255.3M units) as AI-led memory crisis and escalating component costs weighed on end demand. Memory pricing pressure is also coming from Toshiba capacity increase and CXMT DRAM progress. HBM supply remains tight with Micron opening its second Taiwan advanced-packaging plant. Memory complex weakness: WDC/STX/SNDK -5% premarket following Hynix/Samsung Korea session.

bullets.title: Midterm election risk: both outcomes seen as higher-for-longer rates; AI regulation key swing factor
bullets.body: Jefferies flags that fiscal/debt ceiling risks persist under both split Congress and Dem-sweep scenarios, both leading to higher-for-longer rates. A Dem sweep would push AI regulation and curtail AI capex while raising taxes and reversing OBBB incentives, adding pressure to an already stressed AI capex cycle. State capitalism and strategic holdings in rare earths/critical minerals favored under Trump continuation.

bullets.title: Piper Sandler: 15-year tech capex cycle boosting potential GDP; real rates need to be higher
bullets.body: Piper Sandler argues cloud infrastructure investments predating the GPT era are broadly boosting productivity, margins, and potential GDP, with R&D already in place pointing to productivity returning toward early-2000s highs within a few years. The implication: strengthening potential GDP means the Fed needs higher real rates to control inflation, leaving the current accommodative stance misaligned with fundamentals.

bullets.title: Jefferies stagflation warning: price shock becoming demand shock; retail sales/PPI today key test
bullets.body: Jefferies warns the inflation shock may destroy demand more than markets expect. Core services ex-housing running at 4.6% annualized; Republican economic approval collapsed 35ppts Jan-Oct; Beige Book shows broad consumer trading down. The 10Y yield reversal lower after CPI suggests the market is shifting focus from inflation to growth destruction. September PPI and retail sales (expected +0.4% MoM) due today are a critical test of the stagflation thesis.

bullets.title: SaaS valuations 40% below 3Y average; cloud/AI checks still positive into 3Q earnings
bullets.body: Mizuho and Wolfe both flag that NTM EV/Sales multiples are 40% below 3-year averages with IGV returning only 6.3% YTD vs. S&P +15.1%. Despite the discount, cloud/consumption data is strong with AI adoption robust. Mizuho raises MSFT PT to $600, NOW to $170, TEAM to $235; cybersecurity remains top customer priority with 7% NTM budget growth accelerating per Citi CIO survey (82% of CIOs increasing cyber spend due to enterprise AI).

bullets.title: JPM raises GOOGL Cloud to +100% 3Q, AWS to +40% 2027; META faces $10B legal accrual
bullets.body: JPM pre-earnings estimate revisions: GOOGL Cloud growth raised to +100% in 3Q (from +88%) and +107% in 2027 on TPU inclusion; PT $420→$425, Overweight maintained. AMZN AWS accelerates to +40% in 2027 on OpenAI partnership scaling and GPU reserve pricing up 15% (40-75% YTD for H100/H200/B200/B300); PT $365, Overweight. META records $10B legal expense accrual in 3Q for settlement with 52 state AGs, pushing 2027E total GAAP expenses to $210B (+18% YoY); PT $920, Overweight.

bullets.title: OIl at $95.40 WTI / $104.87 Brent on Strait of Hormuz attacks; nat gas +1.8% ahead of storage
bullets.body: Two ships sunk in the Strait of Hormuz from Iranian projectiles and Houthi infrastructure attacks continue to support crude. WTI +0.3% to $95.40, Brent +1.1% to $104.87. API showed 11.12M barrel crude draw. Freight rates from SoH/Red Sea to Asia hit record $34/barrel representing >40% of WTI price per LSEG. Natural gas +1.8% to $3.256 ahead of EIA storage data; consensus expects +76 Bcf build vs. 5-yr avg +90 Bcf.

bullets.title: 10Y yield at ~5.08-5.19%, Russell 2000 in double-digit drawdown; high yield OAS +59bps over last month
bullets.body: Risk-off is broadening beyond tech: Russell 2000 (IWM) down 11% from peak into double-digit drawdown; High Yield OAS widened +11bps in a single day and +59bps over the past month. European sovereign yields declined sharply (30-year Bunds down 3std deviations), suggesting a flight-to-quality rotation. USD weaker vs. most major currencies. NDX futures down 126bps; RTY futures marginally positive as of early morning.

bullets.title: ASML reaffirms inability to meet full 2027-28 demand; raises 2027 EPS 8% on software/memory upgrade
bullets.body: ASML reiterated it cannot fully meet 2027-28 customer demand despite market valuation concerns. Wolfe raises PT to €2,300 (from €2,200) and UBS raises TP to €2,300 on more durable AI-driven demand. Customers are now discussing capacity requirements through 2029-2030, shifting visibility well beyond 2028. ASML's 2027 EPS estimate raised 8% to €60.8 on accelerating memory demand and strong upgrade activity. VAT reported a record 1.9x book-to-bill with 9+ month lead times and 2027 guidance expected significantly above consensus.

bullets.title: Banking 3Q: WFC/BAC NII inflecting higher; C ROTCE above 11%; MS record WM quarter
bullets.body: Banks broadly showed NII inflection despite trading misses. WFC Q4 NII guide of ~$13B ahead of street; FY27 NII modeled +7-8% on loan growth. BAC NII guidance implies 8%+ 2027 growth vs. consensus 6.4%. C raised ROTCE above 11% with efficiency ratio below 60%. MS posted record WM NNA of +$232B with ISG revenues +18% YoY and ROTCE >20%. JPM remains bullish on the sector; WFC PT $101, C PT $164, BAC PT $61.

bullets.title: NFLX: improving setup into Oct 20 earnings; 18x FY27E EPS vs. 27x historical avg, 6% RIF supports margins
bullets.body: Multiple desks constructive on NFLX ahead of Oct 20 earnings. A 6% workforce reduction (~1k roles) raises 2027 EPS estimates. US price increases (3 months in 3Q, 3 months in 4Q), higher ad rates, and a stronger 2027 content slate (36 sequels + 55 non-sequels vs. 31/36 last year) support the top-line narrative. Jefferies estimates 10+ years of 14%+ EPS growth; NFLX trades at 18x FY27E EPS vs. 27x historical average since 2022.

bullets.title: Hedgeye downgrades TSLA, NVDA to Neutral; flags Russell 2000 and retail investor baskets in drawdown
bullets.body: Hedgeye Risk Range signals downgraded both TSLA and NVDA from Bullish to Neutral. Mega-cap tech (MSFT, AAPL, AMZN, META, GOOGL) and XLK remain Bullish; NFLX and Russell 2000 flagged Bearish. S&P 500 SPX Bullish range 7652-7828; NASDAQ Bullish range 26304-27780. Retail investor basket down 9.3% YTD; retail investors reducing Tech ETF exposure while buying NVDA, SNDK, AVGO, TSM dips.

bullets.title: Data center power/capacity crunch: 65 IT GW under construction, 12.9 GW new capacity expected 2026
bullets.body: Jefferies data center analysis estimates ~65 IT GW of capacity under construction (~140% of installed base) with 361 GW of future announced projects. Realistically, 12.9 GW of new DC capacity expected in 2026 and 18 GW in 2027, with many projects facing delays or cancellation. Venture Global is building a 10 GW behind-the-meter island-mode power network with GE Vernova/Baker Hughes to serve AI compute by 2034. EQIX is accelerating meaningful 2027 capacity from 2028.
